backward_compat_traps.rule: 800GbE keeps the Clause-4 MAC frame, so frames are interoperable end-to-end, BUT the PHY (PAM4, RS-FEC(544,514), multi-lane) is entirely different from 10/100/1000 Mb/s MII/GMII PHYs.
backward_compat_traps.trap: An 800G PHY cannot link to a base-802.3 MII/GMII PHY — only the frames are compatible after both ends are up.

backward_compat_traps.rule: 800GbE can be 8 lanes of 100 Gb/s OR 4 lanes of 200 Gb/s; 802.3df targets 100 Gb/s lanes while 802.3dj adds true 200 Gb/s lanes.
backward_compat_traps.trap: An 8x100G module and a 4x200G module are not directly interoperable at the electrical lane level without a gearbox/retimer.

backward_compat_traps.rule: RS-FEC(544,514) KP4 is mandatory; 802.3dj 200G/lane may add a concatenated inner Hamming(128,120) FEC.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Mismatched FEC schemes between link partners prevent FEC alignment and the link never comes up despite clean SerDes.

backward_compat_traps.rule: 800G PHYs expose only Clause-45 MMDs; there is no Clause-22 BMCR/BMSR.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Legacy management software that pokes Clause-22 register 0/1 will get no response from an 800G PHY.

fields.spec_version: IEEE Std 802.3df-2024 (800 Gigabit Ethernet, approved 16 February 2024)
previous_versions: IEEE Std 802.3ba-2010 — 40 GbE + 100 GbE, multi-lane fiber, introduced the multi-PCS-lane / alignment-marker architecture.
IEEE Std 802.3bj-2014 — 100GBASE-KR4/CR4 backplane + twinax with RS-FEC.
IEEE Std 802.3bs-2017 — 200 GbE + 400 GbE, first PAM4 + RS-FEC(544,514) multi-lane PHYs (200GBASE-*, 400GBASE-*).
IEEE Std 802.3ck-2022 — 100 Gb/s/lane PAM4 electrical (CR/KR/DR), the lane technology underpinning 800GBASE 8x100G.
IEEE Std 802.3df-2024 — 800 Gigabit Ethernet (this spec) using 100 Gb/s lanes.

key_changes.summary: First 800 Gb/s Ethernet. MAC at 800 Gb/s preserving the Clause-4 frame format + min/max frame size; PHY over 8x100G or 4x200G PAM4 lanes at 106.25 GBd with RS-FEC(544,514); BER target 1e-13; PMD variants 800GBASE-DR8/SR8/VR8/2xFR4. Project started Jan 2022; scope split Nov 2022 (1.6T + 200G/lane to 802.3dj); approved 16 Feb 2024.

future_versions_industry_outline.summary: 1.6 Tb/s Ethernet + 200/400/800 Gb/s + 1.6 Tb/s PHYs using 200 Gb/s/lane; split from 802.3df in Nov 2022; timeline targets completion July 2026.
256b/257b x RS-FEC(544,514) (optionally concatenated inner Hamming (128,120)) x PAM4 at ~113.4375 GBd, raising per-lane rate to 200 Gb/s and enabling 4x200G 800GbE + 8x200G 1.6TbE.

fields.version_naming_history_note: IEEE 802.3 amendments use letter suffixes. The high-speed PAM4 lineage is 802.3bs (200/400G, 2017) -> 802.3ck (100G/lane electrical, 2022) -> 802.3df (800G using 100G lanes, 2024) -> 802.3dj (1.6T + 200G/lane, ~2026). The Clause-4 MAC frame format is preserved across all of them.
